title: Contribution gates, RFC cadence, and graceful retirement blueprint for primitives
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Purpose: Establish a pragmatic, low-friction set of contribution gates and an RFC cadence for component and token changes (buttons, tables, charts, color/spacing tokens), and define a non-disruptive retirement process for deprecated primitives. This ticket consolidates earlier ad-hoc practices into a single blueprint that product, engineering, and design teams can follow.

Scope: All visual primitives and behaviour-level components maintained in the design system (tokens, core atoms like Button, Table, Chart primitives). Not included: large surface redesigns that require separate program-level roadmaps.

Goals:
- Reduce noisy or blocking reviews by clarifying minimum submission requirements.
- Make RFCs predictable with a defined cadence and template so engineering and infra work can schedule around design changes (kernel-level behavior, runtime flags, AR/quantization concerns referenced in infra RFCs).
- Provide a safe, observable deprecation path (announcement windows, migration helpers, telemetry hooks, automatic compatibility layers where feasible).

Deliverables:
- Contribution gate checklist (required artifacts for a PR to be accepted).
- RFC cadence and template for changes that affect API/contract/semantics.
- Deprecation timeline template with rollback and telemetry requirements.
- Quick-start onboarding checklist for contributors and maintainers.
acceptance_criteria: A concise contribution checklist exists and is documented in Confluence with examples for token and component changes
An RFC template and recommended cadence (2 week review window) published and linked from the design repo README
Deprecation timeline template includes: announcement window, migration docs, telemetry signals, migration PR checklist, and automatic compatibility fallback guidance
The draft is reviewed and signed off by Design Lead, PM owner, and Platform Engineering representative
At least one pilot deprecation performed using the new blueprint and documented learnings
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Rahman: Initial draft created. Pulled common patterns from past component retirements and infra deprecation notes. Added initial checklist items for tokens and Button variants.

2025-02-14 - Marco Li (Engineering): Noted that runtime behavior changes need an explicit compatibility gate and should trigger an infra RFC if they affect KV cache formats. Added pointer to infra RFC template.

2025-02-18 - Priya Menon (PM): Suggested a 14-day minimum RFC review window for mid-sized changes to allow embed teams to schedule validation. Proposed including a 'customer-impact' classification for each RFC.
2025-02-21 - Design Review Meeting: Agreed to require visual regression test artifacts for any changes to tokens or chart primitives. Action: add example Percy/Chromatic snapshots to the checklist.

2025-02-27 - Liam Carter: Incorporated feedback, added migration helper guidelines (deprecation polyfills, alias tokens) and a sample rollout plan with canary routes and feature flags. Linking draft Confluence page and the repo PR template.

2025-03-01 - Security: Reviewed and flagged that deprecation announcements touching auth UI components should include a dependency check with SSO/SSO flows. Security review marked as recommended for those cases.
2025-03-02 - Aisha Rahman: Updated checklist to require a 'regression impact statement' and a customer_impact field on every RFC. Moving ticket to In Review for cross-org sign-off.
decisions: Require visual regression artifacts for any token or visual primitive change
Establish a 2-week nominal RFC review cadence for medium-impact changes, with an expedited path for P0 security or legal issues
Deprecation must include a minimum 30-day public announcement and a 90-day migration window for externally-consumable primitives, unless waived with cross-functional approval
Introduce a small set of contributor gates that must be met before a PR moves past triage: design spec link, visual diffs, accessibility checklist, migration notes if applicable
